forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: North West Leicestershire has taken none of the £9.7m of housing borrowing budgeted for 2026/27
news_drafts.lead:
North West Leicestershire District Council has not taken out any of the £9.7m of new borrowing it budgeted for 2026/27 for its housing revenue account (HRA), the separate, ring-fenced account for its own housing stock, paid for by rents. The position is set out in the mid-year treasury management report going to the full Council on 17 November.

The report says the same amount has been met from internal borrowing, which means using the council's own cash reserves instead of taking a loan. That saves interest but uses up the cushion. The paper forecasts internal borrowing of £37.84m at 31 March 2027.

On the budgeted loan, the report states: "The Council budgeted to undertake new borrowing of £9.7m for the HRA in the 2026/27 financial year, however, none has so far been undertaken."
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix A - Treasury Management Activity 2026/27 Mid-Year Report

news_drafts.headline: North West Leicestershire has not taken £9.7m of budgeted housing borrowing; internal borrowing rises
news_drafts.lead:
North West Leicestershire District Council has not taken any of the £9.7m of new borrowing it budgeted for its housing revenue account in 2026/27. The account is the separate, ring-fenced one for council housing, paid for by rents. The council's Audit and Governance Committee has the figure in its second-quarter treasury management report for the year.

The report says: "The Council budgeted to undertake new borrowing of £9.7m for the HRA in the 2026/27 financial year, however, none has so far been undertaken." Internal borrowing, which means using the council's own cash reserves to pay for capital spending instead of taking a loan, has risen by the same £9.7m.

Internal borrowing is forecast at £37.84m by the end of 2026/27, compared with £29.43m at 31 March 2026. The report notes that internal borrowing foregoes potential interest income of 4.02%. The committee meets on 11 November 2026.

news_drafts.headline: North West Leicestershire flags housing account sustainability risk as reserves fall
news_drafts.lead: North West Leicestershire's housing account faces sustainability risks as unrestricted reserves—money the council can actually spend—fall to critical levels, the council warned this week. Reserves stand at £1.688m, only 68% above the statutory minimum of £1.000m. Consecutive years of financial pressure have driven this decline, with operating expenditure, the cost of day-to-day running, exceeding forecast by £0.293m in the first quarter of 2026/27 alone. Maintenance costs are running £1.022m over budget due to increased repairs activity and £0.204m in compensation for historic repair failures. The council has cut planned debt repayment by 27%, from £1.319m to £1.000m, to manage the pressure, while allocating £0.735m to building reserves.

findings.paper_title: Council Delivery Plan - Performance Report - 2026/27 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Ashby Leisure Centre and Lido energy and carbon projects are unlikely to be delivered before the end of the financial year, with a detailed feasibility due by the end of Q3
findings.detail: Everyone Active is preparing a more detailed feasibility study that will allow Cabinet to decide whether to proceed. The paper says that study should be completed by the end of Q3, so any project delivery falls into the next financial year.
findings.matters: A capital project moving into the next financial year is a slippage a finance director can track against its budget, and a Cabinet go/no-go decision is still to come.
findings.quote: However, it is unlikely delivery will be completed prior to the end of the financial year.

findings.paper_title: Council Delivery Plan - Performance Report - 2026/27 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund Wave 3 is progressing, targeting approximately 844 properties for energy efficiency and decarbonisation, with additional external funding secured for External Wall Insulation
findings.detail: The paper says additional external funding has been secured to expand External Wall Insulation, and a further bid has been submitted for Solar PV. It says a review of around 400 remaining housing properties is underway to set future investment priorities through to 2030.
findings.matters: A grant-funded housing retrofit programme of this size reduces the council's own capital requirement, and the remaining stock review will show whether further capital is needed.
findings.figures: Approximately 844 properties in Wave 3; around 400 properties under review
findings.quote: Additional external funding has been successfully secured to expand the delivery of External Wall Insulation (EWI) measures, and a further bid has been submitted to secure additional funding for Solar PV installations.

findings.paper_title: Council Delivery Plan - Performance Report - 2026/27 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: The report's financial implications were signed off by the Acting Section 151 Officer
findings.detail: The paper's sign-off block records the Acting Section 151 Officer as having approved the financial implications. The paper does not say when the acting arrangement started or how long it will last.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council will want to know who holds the statutory finance officer role during a period of audit catch-up and budget re-planning.
findings.quote: Signed off by the Acting Section 151 Officer: Yes

findings.paper_title: Council Delivery Plan - Performance Report - 2026/27 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: The 2027/28 budget-setting process has started, and the plan needed updating after the withdrawal of the LGR decision in October 2026
findings.detail: The KPI target for living within means is a zero funding gap. The paper says the timetable is on track and that an initial General Fund position is on the agenda for Cabinet on 27 October. It also notes that the LGR decision for Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland, made in July 2026, has been withdrawn, so district elections will take place in 2027.
findings.matters: A council that has to re-plan its medium-term budget after a reorganisation decision is withdrawn is a signal for lenders and peers on how much the 2027/28 position depends on that outcome.
findings.quote: The budget setting process for 2027/28 has started, the plan needed updating following the withdrawal of the LGR decision in October 2026.

findings.paper_title: Council Delivery Plan - Performance Report - 2026/27 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: The Transformation earmarked reserve opened 2026/27 at £421,578, and Finance forecasts it will not be fully spent by 31 March 2027
findings.detail: The paper gives the reserve's balance brought forward at 1 April 2026 and Finance's Quarter 2 forecast. It notes that Microsoft 365 Copilot licence costs sit in the ICT budget rather than this reserve.
findings.matters: An earmarked reserve that is forecast to be under-spent shows the scale of a programme's unused funding, which a finance director can compare with peers' reserve drawdowns.
findings.quote: Finance’s Quarter 2 forecast is that this reserve will not be fully spent by 31 March 2027.
